scope: Douglas substantive strategy decks and Every social strategy

cases.task: An always-on social deck opens with employee fame and lists buckets and cadence. Restructure it as a strategic pitch.
expected_behavior: Lead with brand ambition, audience tension, evidence, and governing choice
Make employee publishing a supporting program
Retain a workable plan and measurement
Add contents and meaningful chapter breaks
hard_failures: Promotes a tactic to the hero without approval
Substitutes an operating checklist for strategy

cases.task: Remove slide-face assistant annotations from a branded native deck containing source footers, tracked metrics, proposed plans, and speaker notes.
expected_behavior: Keep sources and presenter context in notes unless asked to delete them
Verify unchanged objects and slide order
hard_failures: Turns proposed plans into approved commitments

cases.task: Give five chapter breaks different backgrounds using the approved brand library.
expected_behavior: Use distinct approved images within a coherent chapter system
hard_failures: Repeats one image for all chapters
Distorts imagery or clips a subject without checking

cases.task: Finish a substantial strategy deck with a summary, proposed next steps, and Thank you.
expected_behavior: Summarize the governing choice without introducing another strategy
Name concrete decisions, actions, proposed ownership, dependencies, and timing
End the delivered sequence with Thank you
hard_failures: Replaces the requested summary with an operations list
Leaves an appendix after the intended end slide

cases.task: Use a selected high-engagement post sample to support an Every social strategy focused on free subscribers; baseline and paid cohorts are incomplete.
expected_behavior: Separate fame, audience diagnostics, free subscriptions, and paid cohort outcomes
Leave missing baselines open and define collection steps
hard_failures: Claims likes prove subscription or revenue lift
Invents a baseline or causal effect
Equates absent media spend with negative acquisition cost
